storylines.title: Nine nights built to this one evening, when the effigy finally burns
storylines.observation: Shardiya Navratri began Oct 11 with Ghatasthapana: a sacred kalash installed as Durga's vessel, packed with soil, coins and grain with barley seeds sown beneath it, opening nine nights devoted to nine successive forms of the goddess.
storylines.question: What does it mean to represent one deity's power as nine distinct, separately-named forms rather than one continuous figure?
storylines.hidden_question: Does splitting the goddess into nine stages make an otherwise overwhelming concept graspable, or does the division itself quietly change what's actually being worshipped?
storylines.pattern: a single extended devotion broken into discrete, individually-named stages rather than treated as one continuous observance
storylines.why_now: Tonight the nine nights resolve into a single public act: effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnada burned after sunset, at the Vijay Muhurat - the moment the devotional stages of the past nine days give way to one shared, visible ending.
storylines.location: India and the Hindu diaspora worldwide
storylines.season_or_time_context: Navratri began Oct 11, 2026, runs nine nights to Dussehra Oct 20

history.note: Dussehra / Vijayadashami: the festival closes tonight with Ravan Dahan - burning effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnada - marking Rama's victory and giving the nine separately-named nights a single, visible end.

Day nine belongs to Siddhidatri - the final form, said to grant all eight siddhis and already fully accomplished rather than seeking anything further. Many families mark the day with Kanya Pujan, honoring young girls as living embodiments of the goddess.

Day eight belongs to Mahagauri - depicted radiant and fair-skinned after penance purified her, worshipped for purity and the dissolving of past wrongs. Purple is a common colour for the day; coconut the customary offering.

storylines.title: Each march is bigger than the last. The government's answer is still "end of October"
storylines.observation: Since mid-September, French students have blockaded or closed high schools and university sites over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and crumbling buildings. PM Lecornu's Oct 4 letter deferred actual decisions to "fin octobre" - month's end.
storylines.question: What does it mean when a protest's turnout keeps growing precisely because the official response keeps being deferred?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the government waiting out a movement that's actually accelerating, or has it simply lost the ability to read how big this has become?
storylines.pattern: an official response that defers the substance of an answer past the span of attention the problem is currently getting
storylines.why_now: Oct 17's 'convergence des luttes' - students joined by gilets jaunes, nurses and retirees - drew the movement's largest turnout yet: 800,000 by organizers' count, 550,000 by the Interior Ministry's, both well above the already-disputed Oct 13 figures (480k/161.5k). The gap between the two counts has grown alongside the protest itself.
storylines.season_or_time_context: protests began mid-September 2026, ongoing; Oct 17 'convergence des luttes' drew allied groups beyond students

history.note: Oct 17's broadened 'convergence des luttes' march - students plus gilets jaunes, nurses, retirees - drew 800,000 (organizers) to 550,000 (Interior Ministry), the movement's biggest and most disputed count yet.

The Oct 13 numbers: Interior Ministry counted about 161,500 marchers nationwide, organizers say 480,000. 214 high schools were shut; 20 education staff were hurt that day alone, 147 since the movement began.

storylines.title: He said he deserved 8 Nobel Peace Prizes. The committee gave this year's to someone he'd never heard of
storylines.observation: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize went Oct 9 to Navi Pillay, the 85-year-old South African jurist and former UN human rights chief, honoring decades of institution-building in international law. Trump, who had expected to win, called the choice 'disgraceful.'
storylines.question: What does it mean when a prize for peace becomes, for the loudest non-winner, evidence of a personal snub rather than a judgment about the work itself?
storylines.hidden_question: Is Trump's reaction really about this prize, or about what it means that an institution he can't control gets to decide who counts as having built peace?
storylines.pattern: an institutional honor read by its most prominent non-recipient as a personal verdict rather than a judgment about the work
storylines.why_now: The same day Trump called Pillay someone he'd 'never heard of' and said he should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes instead, his administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court - the institution Pillay herself once served as a judge.
storylines.season_or_time_context: prize announced Oct 9, 2026; ceremony Dec 10 in Oslo

history.note: Pillay escalated in an Oct 14 interview: she called the ICC sanctions 'illegal,' predicted Netanyahu will stand trial, and called Israel's 'Goebbels applauding from hell' jab and Netanyahu's 'bigot' label 'hurtful and insulting' - a prize reaction now a three-way fight.

Trump posted that he knew 'nothing about this woman' and that she 'very obviously, hates Israel'; at a rally he added 'congratulations anyway.' Pillay, told of this, called him a 'mysterious figure' - the same day the US sanctioned the ICC, where she once sat as a judge.
